original_question: Let S be a finite simple nonabelian group that is not isomorphic to any group 2B2(q). A nonidentity automorphism x of S is called a τ-automorphism if every two conjugates of x in ⟨x, Inn(S)⟩ generate a subgroup of order not divisible by 3. If S admits a τ-automorphism, we call S a τ-group. (a) List all τ-groups up to isomorphism. (b) Do τ-automorphisms of odd order exist?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.111 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of the Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation and in substance reproduces it almost verbatim: it has the same excluded family ^2B_2(q), the same definition of a tau-automorphism via pairs of conjugates inside <x, Inn(S)>, the same definition of a tau-group, and the same two tasks: classify all tau-groups up to isomorphism and ask whether odd-order tau-automorphisms exist.
missing_details: Make explicit that x is an element of Aut(S), i.e. a nonidentity automorphism of S.
Spell out Inn(S) as the inner automorphism group of S.
Clarify that the conjugacy condition is taken inside the subgroup <x, Inn(S)>, not inside all of Aut(S).
For a fully stand-alone statement, specify that ^2B_2(q) denotes the Suzuki simple groups, with q = 2^(2m+1) >= 8.
Add the official problem label from the paper: Problem 21.111.
refined_question: Classify, up to isomorphism, all finite nonabelian simple groups S other than the Suzuki groups ^2B_2(q) (where q = 2^(2m+1) >= 8) for which there exists a nonidentity automorphism x in Aut(S) such that for every g,h in <x, Inn(S)>, the subgroup <x^g, x^h> has order not divisible by 3; such an automorphism x is called a tau-automorphism, and such a group S is called a tau-group. Also determine whether any tau-automorphism can have odd order.
